newsitem.title: USA: Anchorage mayor re-elected; bond issues pass.
newsitem.headline: Anchorage mayor re-elected; bond issues pass.

text.p: Rick Mystrom was elected Tuesday to a second three-year term as mayor of Anchorage, handily beating a a more conservative opponent, preliminary results showed Wednesday.
Mystrom, a moderate Republican, won 54 percent of the vote against 42 percent for conservative Republican Tom Fink, who was trying to regain the seat he held from late 1987 to early 1994.
Eight other candidates split the remainder of the vote in the city's non-partisan mayoral election.

By a 62-37 percent margin voters in Alaska's largest city also approved a ballot measure that amends the municipal charter to require a 60 percent vote in order to establish or raise a sales tax. Anchorage has no sales tax and until now the municipal charter has required only a majority vote to establish such a tax.
In addition, voters approved $52.68 million of the total $55.645 million in municipal bond items that were on the ballot, according to the preliminary results.
The bonds were for school improvements, road and drainage projects, emergency medical service enhancements and parks and recreation projects.
Chuck Albrecht, a spokesman for the Mystrom administration, said the bonds were for popular projects.
"Roads always do well. Fire protection does well. We are very grateful for the parks and rec bonds, because parks and rec bonds don't always do well," he said.
In the non-partisan election for three school board seats, a trio of conservatives who ran on a unified slate were easily defeated by more liberal candidates.
